From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 6 May 2029 10:05:42 -0700
Subject: RE: [P0] us-west-2a — 10x latency + 502 surge

Quick telemetry snapshot from the runtime:
- Detected ~09:01 PDT: intermittent heartbeat loss between inference pool us-west-2a and shared KV-cache cluster kv-west-2 (node kvc-7).
- From 09:01–09:45 the serving runtime saw elevated KV cache miss rate (x5 baseline) causing synchronous fallbacks to remote param store and cold start of contexts — explains 1.2–2.0s tails.
- Concurrently our edge LB saw increased 502 responses from a small subset of instances that reported kvc-7 timeouts.

Actions taken:
- At 09:50 PDT we enabled an emergency canary routing rule for Stratus routing to us-west-1 (5% of traffic) and observed latency drop for those requests.
- At 10:00 PDT we expanded the diversion to 40% and continued validation.
- We are NOT seeing global control-plane failures, this appears to be localized to the kv-west-2 attachment in us-west-2a.

Recommendation:
- Immediate: pin Stratus traffic to us-west-1 for the next 3 hours (rollback window 18:00 PDT) while we replace kvc-7 and resync the cluster.
- Medium: replace kvc-7, resync KV cluster, validate hedged reads/healthchecks for kvc cluster.
- Postmortem: run an RCA on why heartbeat and healthchecks didn't trigger earlier alarm thresholds.

Attachment: diagnostic-kv-log.txt (contains truncated logs: TTL expirations, socket errors)

— Rishi
Sr. SRE, Serving Runtime
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
